code.name: Ohio Revised Code
code.edition: Ohio Revised Code as the Ohio Legislative Service Commission's site (codes.ohio.gov) prints it on 2026-11-07; each section shows its own effective date and latest legislation (for example 3505.33 effective September 30, 2025; 3515.011 effective July 4, 1984)

oh-3505.citation: Ohio Rev. Code ch. 3505 (Ballots; Canvass), sections 3505.33 (declaration of results, tie votes), 3505.34 (canvass for state executive offices by the general assembly), 3505.35 (canvass by the secretary of state), 3505.36 (multi-county districts), 3505.37 (subdivision in more than one county)

oh-3513.citation: Ohio Rev. Code ch. 3513 (Primary elections), section 3513.22 (canvass and certification of votes)

oh-3515.citation: Ohio Rev. Code ch. 3515 (Recount; contest of elections), sections 3515.01 (eligibility for recount), 3515.011 (recounts ordered by board), 3515.03 (application contents, deposit, stop request), 3515.07 (charges), 3515.071 (expenses), 3515.14 (judgment on contest)

ties.applies_to: the offices of governor and lieutenant governor (as joint candidates), secretary of state, auditor of state, treasurer of state and attorney general, at a regular state election (section 3505.34)
ties.steps: the president of the senate canvasses the abstracts before a majority of the members of each house of the general assembly in the first week of the regular session after the election; if two or more candidates (or sets of joint candidates for governor and lieutenant governor) receive the largest and an equal number of votes, one of them is declared elected by a majority of the votes of all the members of the senate and the house of representatives
ties.who: the general assembly (senate and house voting together)

sources.quote: If two or more candidates for election to the same office, or two or more sets of joint candidates for governor and lieutenant governor, receive the largest and an equal number of votes, one of them, or one set of joint candidates for governor and lieutenant governor, shall be declared elected to such office by a majority of the votes of all of the members of the senate and the house of representatives of the general assembly.

ties.note: Section 3505.35(A) also says a tie in a statewide election is resolved by lot by the secretary of state and names joint candidates for governor, but it adds that the secretary of state's declaration, for these five offices, is only for fixing the time of the commencement of the recount-application period (it quotes section 3515.02); so the general assembly's canvass is read as the one that decides these five offices [inferred]. The Ohio Constitution was not read.

ties.applies_to: elections in which electors throughout the entire state voted: U.S. senator and presidential electors, and other offices chosen statewide (section 3505.35(A)); the five executive offices above are decided under 3505.34
ties.steps: the secretary of state canvasses the county abstracts and, if two or more candidates for the same office receive the largest and an equal number of votes, resolves the tie by lot

sources.quote: shall determine and declare the results of all elections in which electors throughout the entire state voted. If two or more candidates for election to the same office, or two or more sets of joint candidates for governor and lieutenant governor, receive the largest and an equal number of votes, such tie shall be resolved by lot by the secretary of state.

ties.note: The text says "all elections in which electors throughout the entire state voted" and does not name U.S. senator, presidential electors or any statewide judicial office; reading it as covering them is an inference. The mention of presidential electors' meeting in section 3505.39 (where a tie among the electors appointing replacement electors is decided by the governor by lot) is a different matter and was not recorded as a rule.

ties.applies_to: an office determined by the electors of one county, or of a district or subdivision within one county (general or special election; section 3505.33), for example a U.S. House district, a legislative district or a local office lying within one county
ties.steps: the county board of elections canvasses the returns and declares the result; if more than the number of candidates to be elected received the largest and an equal number of votes, the chairperson of the board resolves the tie by lot in the presence of a majority of the board's members
ties.who: the chairperson of the county board of elections

sources.quote: If more than the number of candidates to be elected to an office received the largest and an equal number of votes, such tie shall be resolved by lot by the chairperson of the board in the presence of a majority of the members of the board.

ties.note: The text covers "the results of the elections determined by the electors of such county or of a district or subdivision within such county" and does not name federal, state or local offices; mapping it to U.S. House, state legislative and local offices is an inference. Municipal charters were not read.

ties.applies_to: an office or issue voted on only by the electors of a district made up of more than one county but less than all counties (section 3505.36), for example a U.S. House or legislative district spanning counties
ties.steps: the board of elections of the most populous county in the district canvasses the abstracts of all the district's counties; if more than the number of candidates to be elected receive the largest and an equal number of votes, the chairman of that board resolves the tie by lot in the presence of all of its members
ties.who: the chairman of the board of elections of the most populous county in the district

sources.quote: If more than the number of candidates to be elected to an office receive the largest number and an equal number of votes, such tie shall be resolved by lot by the chairman of such board in the presence of all of the members of such board.

ties.note: Section 3505.36 speaks of "a district comprised of more than one county" and names no kind of office; mapping it to U.S. House, state legislative and district offices is an inference.

ties.applies_to: an office voted on only by the electors of a subdivision located in more than one county (section 3505.37)
ties.steps: the board of elections of the county holding the major portion of the subdivision's population canvasses the parts of abstracts from each county; if more than the number of candidates to be elected receive the largest and an equal number of votes, the chairman of that board resolves the tie by lot in the presence of a majority of its members
ties.who: the chairman of the board of elections of the county containing the major portion of the subdivision's population

sources.quote: If more than the number of candidates to be elected to an office receive the largest number and an equal number of votes, such tie shall be resolved by lot by the chairman of such board in the presence of a majority of the members of such board.

ties.note: State general law only; municipal, township and school charters or special laws were not read.

ties.applies_to: a primary election (section 3513.22): county, district or subdivision contests canvassed by a board of elections, and contests voted on throughout the state canvassed by the secretary of state
ties.steps: if more than the number of persons to be nominated for or elected to an office received the largest and an equal number of votes, the tie is resolved by lot: by the chairperson of the county board in the presence of a majority of its members (county, district, subdivision), or by the secretary of state in the presence of the governor, the auditor of state and the attorney general (statewide)
ties.who: the chairperson of the board of elections, or for a statewide primary the secretary of state before the governor, auditor of state and attorney general

sources.quote: If more than the number of persons to be nominated for or elected to an office received the largest and an equal number of votes, the tie shall be resolved by lot by the secretary of state in the presence of the governor, the auditor of state, and the attorney general, who at the request of the secretary of state shall assemble to witness the drawing of the lot.

If more than the number of persons to be nominated for or elected to an office received the largest and an equal number of votes, the tie shall be resolved by lot by the chairperson of the board in the presence of a majority of the members of the board.

ties.applies_to: a tie found by the court in a contest of an election (section 3515.14); the section does not apply to a federal office, whose contests are under federal law (section 3515.08, not quoted)
ties.steps: if the court in a contest decides that the election resulted in a tie vote, the decision is certified to the board of elections having jurisdiction, and the board publicly determines by lot which of the persons is declared elected
ties.who: the board of elections, on the court's certification

sources.quote: If the court decides that the election resulted in a tie vote, such decision shall be certified to the board of elections having jurisdiction and said board shall publicly determine by lot which of such persons shall be declared elected.

ties.note: This is the route after an election contest, recorded because it says what happens to a tie; the primary route above is the ordinary one.

ties.applies_to: a contest of the election of a member of the general assembly (section 3515.14)
ties.steps: in a contest of a member of the general assembly the court does not pronounce judgment; a transcript of the testimony and evidence is filed with the clerk or executive secretary of the branch the contestee was declared elected to, and that branch determines the election and qualification of its own members
ties.who: the house or senate to which the contestee was declared elected

sources.quote: in the case of the contest of election of a member of the general assembly such judgment shall not be pronounced by the court but a transcript of all testimony taken and all evidence adduced in such contest shall be filed with the clerk or executive secretary of the branch of the legislative body to which the contestee was declared elected, which shall determine the election and qualification of its own members.

ties.note: This is the contest route only; it is not the rule for a tie at the canvass (see the county and district rules).

ties.applies_to: a question or issue submitted to the voters
ties.steps: no provision found saying what a tie on a question or issue does
ties.note: Read for the words "tie", "by lot" and "equal number of votes": chapter 3505 (canvass, all of it as fetched), chapter 3513 (primaries) and chapter 3515 (recount and contest of elections). The tie provisions found speak of candidates and persons; none mentions a question or issue. An absence cannot be confirmed from these chapters alone; chapters 3519 (initiative and referendum) and the local-option chapters were not read.

threshold.conditions: county or municipal election; the board of elections orders the recount
threshold.in_words: a margin under one-half of one percent of the total vote in a county or municipal election (the winner's lead does not reach one-half of one percent)

recounts.cost_bearer: county (expense paid from the county treasury as other board expenses; section 3515.071)
recounts.waiver: the declared losing candidate or nominee may file a written request with the board, before the recount commences, to stop it from commencing; where several losing candidates are entitled to a recount, each must file the request (section 3515.03)

sources.quote: If the number of votes cast in any county or municipal election for the declared winning nominee, candidate, question, or issue does not exceed the number of votes cast for the declared defeated nominee, candidate, question, or issue by a margin of one-half of one per cent or more of the total vote, the appropriate board of elections shall order a recount

If the board of elections in a county orders a recount in any county or municipal election pursuant to section 3515.011 of the Revised Code, the expense of the recount shall be paid from the county treasury in the same manner as other expenses of the board under section 3501.17 of the Revised Code.

recounts.note: "does not exceed ... by a margin of one-half of one per cent or more" is read as: recount when the lead is less than one-half of one percent (inclusive false) [inferred]. The text names "nominee" (primary) and "question, or issue" (measure) as well as candidates. A state legislative or other district wholly inside one county may be a "county" or a "district" election; the statute does not say [inferred].

threshold.conditions: district election; the secretary of state orders the recount
threshold.in_words: a margin under one-half of one percent of the total vote in a district election

recounts.cost_bearer: state (paid from funds appropriated to the secretary of state; section 3515.071)
recounts.waiver: the declared losing candidate or nominee may file a written request with the board, before the recount commences, to stop it from commencing (section 3515.03)

sources.quote: If the number of votes cast in any district election for the declared winning nominee, candidate, question, or issue does not exceed the number of votes cast for the declared defeated nominee, candidate, question, or issue by a margin of one-half of one per cent or more of the total vote, the secretary of state shall order a recount
If the secretary of state orders a recount as provided in section 3515.011 of the Revised Code, the expense of the recount shall be paid from funds appropriated to the secretary of state

recounts.note: "district election" is not defined in the section; mapping it to U.S. House and state legislative districts that span counties is an inference (section 3515.02 uses "a district comprised of more than one county but less than all of the counties of the state").

threshold.conditions: statewide election; the secretary of state orders the recount
threshold.in_words: a margin under one-fourth of one percent of the total vote in a statewide election

recounts.cost_bearer: state (paid from funds appropriated to the secretary of state; section 3515.071)
recounts.waiver: the declared losing candidate or nominee may file a written request with the board, before the recount commences, to stop it from commencing (section 3515.03)

sources.quote: If the number of votes cast in any statewide election for the declared winning nominee, candidate, question, or issue does not exceed the number of votes cast for the declared defeated nominee, candidate, question, or issue by a margin of one-fourth of one per cent or more of the total vote, the secretary of state shall order a recount

recounts.note: Applies to U.S. senator, presidential electors, the statewide executive offices and statewide issues by the words "any statewide election" [inferred for the kinds]. Any recount of presidential electors must be completed not later than six days before the electors meet (section 3515.041, not quoted).

threshold.in_words: no margin condition: any candidate who was not declared elected, or any person for whom votes were cast in a primary and who was not declared nominated, may apply

who_may_request: any person for whom votes were cast in a primary for nomination who was not declared nominated
any person who was a candidate at a general, special or primary election who was not declared elected
recounts.cost_bearer: the applicant: a deposit of fifty dollars per listed precinct, from which the board deducts its per-precinct charge (between five and fifty dollars per precinct recounted); no charge is deducted if the applicant is declared nominated or elected, or if the applicant's votes in the precinct rise by more than four percent (sections 3515.03 and 3515.07; the dollar amounts are adjusted every odd-numbered year under 3515.072)
recounts.waiver: none: the charge is waived in the cases stated, not by a margin

sources.quote: Any person who was a candidate at a general, special, or primary election for election to an office or postion who was not declared elected may file with the board of a county a written application for a recount of the votes cast at such election in any precinct in such county for all candidates for election to such office or position.

the person filing the application shall, at the same time, deposit with the board of elections fifty dollars in currency, bank money order, bank cashier's check, or certified check for each precinct so listed as security for the payment of charges for making the recount applied for
provided that the charges per precinct so fixed shall not be more than fifty or less than five dollars for each precinct the votes of which were recounted.

recounts.note: The filing deadline is five days after the board or the secretary of state declares the result (section 3515.02, not quoted). The statute does not exclude federal offices from the recount chapter (only from the contest in 3515.08), so the kinds list includes them [inferred]. Dollar amounts are the base amounts in the section's text and are adjusted by the secretary of state under 3515.072.

threshold.in_words: no margin condition: any group of five or more qualified electors who voted on the losing side of a declared result may apply

who_may_request: a group of five or more qualified electors who state that they voted Yes and the question or issue was declared defeated or rejected, or voted No and it was declared carried or adopted
recounts.cost_bearer: the applicant group (chairman is the applicant): the same fifty-dollar-per-precinct deposit and per-precinct charges (sections 3515.03 and 3515.07); no charge is deducted for a precinct where the applicants' side gains more than four percent or the result is reversed

sources.quote: Any group of five or more qualified electors may file with the board of a county a written application for a recount of the votes cast at an election in any precinct in such county upon any question or issue, provided that the members of such group shall state in such application either that they voted "Yes" or in favor of such question or issue and that such question or issue was declared defeated or rejected

unread.what: Ohio Constitution provisions on ties for governor and other officers, chapter 3519 (initiative and referendum), local-option and special-election chapters, municipal and township charters
unread.reason: not part of the election-code chapters on canvass (3505), primary canvass (3513) and recount (3515) that were read; state general law only for local offices

notes: Read in full as fetched: chapter 3515 (all of it), chapter 3505 (searched for tie, by lot and equal number of votes; sections 3505.33 to 3505.37 read whole), chapter 3513 (searched; section 3513.22 read whole). The three pages were each fetched once from codes.ohio.gov on 2026-11-07.

Ohio sends a tie for governor and the four other executive offices to the general assembly, not to a lot; the statewide lot in 3505.35(A) applies to every other statewide election and, for the five executive offices, is only a preliminary declaration.
